summary: Defines the L2VPN Network Model (L2NM), a YANG model for managing the provisioning of Layer 2 VPN services within a network such as a service provider network. It complements the L2VPN Service Model (L2SM) by offering a network-centric view, meant for use by a network controller. It is a standards-track specification.

plainLanguage.summary: YANG is a language for describing the configuration and state of network devices so that software can read and write it. RFC 9291 uses YANG to describe a Layer 2 VPN the way the service provider sees it: which routers take part, which customer sites attach where, and how the pseudowires between them are signalled.

questions: what is the l2vpn network model
yang model for layer 2 vpn provisioning
subtitle: A YANG data model that lets a network controller manage Layer 2 VPN services from the provider's side.

tldr.problem: A customer orders a Layer 2 VPN through a service model that describes the service from the outside, but that model says nothing about how the provider's own network should be built.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines the ietf-l2vpn-ntw YANG module, a network view with VPN services, VPN nodes and VPN network accesses, plus an ietf-ethernet-segment module and two IANA modules of identities for encapsulation and pseudowire types.
tldr.outcome: A service orchestrator can hand a network controller a structured description of the service to build, and the controller can derive the configuration for each device. The model also exposes the operational state of the service.

today: RFC 9291 is a Proposed Standard, published in September 2022. No RFC obsoletes it and no RFC updates it, so it is the published network data model for Layer 2 VPN services.

sections.title: A Network View of Layer 2 VPN Service
sections.content:
RFC 8466 defines an L2VPN Service Model (L2SM) YANG data model that can be used between customers and service providers for ordering Layer 2 Virtual Private Network services. This document complements the L2SM by creating a network-centric view of the service, the L2VPN Network Model (L2NM).

The document also defines the initial versions of two IANA-maintained modules that define a set of identities of BGP Layer 2 encapsulation types and pseudowire types. These types are used in the L2NM to identify a Layer 2 encapsulation type as a function of the signalling option used to deliver an L2VPN service. Relying on IANA-maintained modules is meant to give more flexibility in handling new types, rather than being limited by a set of identities defined in the L2NM itself. Section 8.3 defines another YANG module to manage Ethernet Segments, which are required for instantiating Ethernet VPNs. References to Ethernet segments created with that module can be included in the L2NM for EVPNs.

The L2NM can be exposed, for example, by a network controller to a service controller inside the service provider's network. In particular, the model can be used in the interface between the entity that interacts directly with the customer, the service orchestrator, and the entity in charge of network orchestration, the network controller or orchestrator, by allowing more network-centric information to be included. The L2NM supports capabilities such as exposing operational parameters, transport protocol selection and precedence, and it can also serve as a multi-domain orchestration interface.

The model is scoped for a variety of Layer 2 VPNs: Virtual Private LAN Service (VPLS), Virtual Private Wire Service (VPWS), and various flavours of EVPN, including VPWS EVPN, Provider Backbone Bridging Combined with Ethernet VPNs, EVPN over MPLS, and EVPN over VXLAN. It is designed to support future Layer 2 VPN flavours and procedures, such as pseudowire resilience or multi-segment pseudowires. A set of examples is given in Appendix A. The document uses the common Virtual Private Network YANG module of RFC 9181, and the data models conform to the Network Management Datastore Architecture of RFC 8342.
sections.plainLanguage: The L2SM is what the customer sees: the sites, the bandwidth, the service. The L2NM is what the provider sees: which provider edge routers are involved, which signalling protocol carries the pseudowires between them, and which Ethernet segments the sites attach through. The two are separate on purpose, because the internal view should not be exposed to customers.

sections.title: Where the L2NM Sits in Orchestration
sections.content:
The reference architecture expands the orchestration box of the L2SM architecture into three functional components: service orchestration, network orchestration and domain orchestration. Attachment from a customer edge to a provider edge is achieved through a bearer with a Layer 2 connection on top. The bearer refers to properties of the attachment that are below Layer 2, while the connection refers to Layer 2 protocol-oriented properties. The domain orchestration and config manager roles may be performed by SDN controllers, and the device configuration is delivered with NETCONF or the command line.

The customer may use various means to request a service that triggers the instantiation of an L2NM, for example the L2SM itself or more abstract models such as an IP Connectivity Provisioning Profile, an enhanced VPN service or an IETF network slice service. Both the L2SM and the L2NM may also be used in the context of the Abstraction and Control of TE Networks framework, where the customer network controller talks to a multi-domain service coordinator and the L2NM is passed down to domain controllers and their provisioning network controllers.

The L2NM is not a customer service model. The internal view of the service may be mapped to an external view that is visible to customers, which is the L2SM. The L2NM can be fed with inputs requested by customers that typically rely on an L2SM template: some parts of the L2SM module map directly into the L2NM, while other parts are generated as a function of the requested service and local guidelines. Finally, there are parts local to the service provider that do not map directly to the L2SM at all.
sections.plainLanguage: The chain runs from the customer order to the service orchestrator, then to the network controller, then to per-domain controllers that configure the individual routers. The L2NM is the document that travels along that chain between the service orchestrator and the network controller.

sections.title: The Ethernet Segment Module
sections.content:
The ietf-ethernet-segment module is used to manage a set of Ethernet segments in the context of an EVPN service. An Ethernet Segment is the set of Ethernet links used by a customer site, a device or network, to connect to one or more provider edge routers. The module has a container of Ethernet segments, each keyed by a name that uniquely identifies it within the service provider network, and a typedef es-ref is defined so that other modules can refer to a segment by name.

The esi-type node indicates the Ethernet Segment Identifier type, as discussed in Section 5 of RFC 7432. Six types are supported. Type 0 is configured directly by the VPN service provider. Type 1 is generated automatically from the IEEE 802.1AX Link Aggregation Control Protocol. Type 2 is generated automatically and determined by the Layer 2 bridge protocol. Type 3 is a MAC-based value that can be generated automatically or configured. Type 4 is generated or configured from the Router ID, and the router-id supplied at the VPN node level can be used to derive one. Type 5 is generated or configured from the Autonomous System number, and the local-autonomous-system supplied in the global parameters can be used to derive one. Automatically generated values are read back through auto-ethernet-segment-identifier.

The esi-redundancy-mode node specifies the EVPN redundancy mode for the segment, either Single-Active or All-Active. The df-election container holds the parameters of the Designated Forwarder election, including the election method and the wait timer, and a revertive leaf that overrides the default behaviour of taking the role back when the former Designated Forwarder returns. The split-horizon-filtering leaf controls the activation of split horizon filtering for the segment, and the pbb container holds data specific to Provider Backbone Bridging, such as a backbone source MAC address. Finally, a list of members records the network elements and interfaces that belong to the segment.
sections.plainLanguage: An Ethernet segment is the bundle of links a customer site uses to reach the provider network. The module names those bundles and records the identifier that tells the network the links belong together. The identifier can be set by hand or derived from something already known, such as the router's own ID or the AS number.

sections.title: The Overall Shape of the L2NM
sections.content:
The ietf-l2vpn-ntw module is used to manage L2VPNs within a service provider network. It can be used to create, modify, delete and retrieve L2VPN services in a network controller, and it is designed to minimize the amount of customer-related information it carries.

The module uses two main containers. The vpn-profiles container is used by the provider to define and maintain a set of common VPN profiles that apply to VPN services, and it holds identifiers rather than the policies themselves, because the exact definition of each profile is local to the provider. The identifiers cover external connectivity, encryption, quality of service, Bidirectional Forwarding Detection, forwarding and routing profiles, and each is defined with default-deny-write tagging.

The vpn-services container maintains the set of L2VPN services managed in the provider network. A new service is created by adding an instance of vpn-service, which is the data structure that abstracts the service. Each service is uniquely identified by a vpn-id, which is only meaningful locally within the network controller. Under each service sit its global parameters profiles, its VPN nodes, and each VPN node holds the VPN network accesses where customer traffic enters.

Within a VPN service, the vpn-type node says which kind of Layer 2 VPN it is: VPLS, VPWS, VPWS EVPN, Provider Backbone Bridging EVPN, MPLS-based EVPN or VXLAN-based EVPN. The type is used as a condition for the presence of some other data nodes. The vpn-service-topology node gives the network topology as hub-spoke, any-to-any or custom. The signaling-type node records which signalling is used to set up the pseudowires, and bgp-ad-enabled controls whether BGP auto-discovery is enabled. The underlay-transport node describes the preference for the transport technology that will carry the service's traffic, either as an abstract transport instance or as an ordered list of actual protocols. A status container tracks both administrative and operational status with timestamps, so a service that is declared created at the service layer but still inactive at the network layer can be spotted.
sections.plainLanguage: The model has two halves: a library of reusable profiles that the provider defines once, and a list of services built from those profiles. Each service names its kind, its topology and its signalling, and each holds the provider routers that take part in it.

sections.title: VPN Services, VPN Nodes and Network Accesses
sections.content:
A vpn-node is an abstraction that represents a set of policies applied on a network node and that belongs to a single VPN service. It carries an identifier, an optional network element identifier, a role such as any-to-any, spoke or hub, and a router ID that uniquely identifies the router within an AS. It lists the global parameter profiles that are active at that node, and values set here override the ones set at the service level.

A vpn-network-access represents an entry point to a VPN service, and holds the parameters that describe the access information for the traffic that belongs to a particular L2VPN. It carries an identifier, the interface it is bound to, a pointer to the active global parameters profile at the VPN node level, and its own status. Unlike the L2SM, the L2NM does not model the customer site itself; only the point that receives traffic from the site, the provider side of the customer-to-provider connection, is covered.

Inside the network access, a connection container groups the Layer 2 connectivity from which the traffic of the VPN arrives, such as the encapsulation type, link aggregation groups and split horizon, and it supports tag manipulation operations such as tag rewrite. It deliberately excludes the physical-specific configuration, which is assumed to be handled by device modules, and this is also meant to avoid manipulating global parameters at the service level and lowering the risk of impacting other services that share the same physical interface. A reference to the bearer is maintained so that the link between the L2SM and the L2NM can be kept when both are used in one deployment.

A group container groups network accesses by assigning them the same identifier, and its precedence attribute distinguishes primary from secondary accesses in a service with several. The same container is used to identify the link of an Ethernet segment by allocating the same Ethernet Segment Identifier. The ethernet-service-oam container carries information about the service operations, administration and maintenance, and the service container specifies the service parameters such as quality of service and multicast for a given network access.
sections.plainLanguage: A VPN node is a provider router taking part in one VPN. A network access is the place on that router where a customer site plugs in. The network access can point at a group of sibling accesses with a precedence order, which is how a site with two links says which one is primary.

sections.title: Signalling Options and BGP Auto-Discovery
sections.content:
The bgp-auto-discovery container holds the information needed to activate BGP auto-discovery, which lets the routers find each other and exchange the information needed to build the service. The signaling-option container records how the pseudowires are set up.

Three signalling options are supported. Under bgp-signaling there are two flavours. The l2vpn-bgp flavour is a multipoint VPLS that uses a BGP control plane. The evpn-bgp flavour is also a multipoint VPLS with a BGP control plane, but it adds the EVPN features and related parameters. Under ldp-signaling, a multipoint VPLS uses a mesh of LDP-signalled pseudowires. Under l2tp-signaling, the pseudowires are L2TP-signalled.

Which combinations are allowed depends on the type of service. VPLS and VPWS allow L2TP signalling, LDP signalling or BGP signalling with the L2VPN flavour. The four EVPN flavours, VPWS EVPN, Provider Backbone Bridging EVPN, MPLS-based EVPN and VXLAN-based EVPN, allow only BGP signalling with the EVPN flavour. The L2NM uses the IANA-maintained modules for BGP Layer 2 encapsulation and pseudowire types to identify the encapsulation and pseudowire types, which lets new types be added without changing the L2NM itself.
sections.plainLanguage: The service type limits the choices. A plain VPLS can be built with L2TP, with LDP, or with BGP. An EVPN of any flavour must use BGP, because EVPN needs the extra information BGP carries.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The YANG modules define schemas for data designed to be accessed with network management protocols such as NETCONF or RESTCONF. The lowest NETCONF layer is the secure transport layer, where the mandatory-to-implement secure transport is Secure Shell, and the lowest RESTCONF layer is HTTPS, where the mandatory-to-implement secure transport is TLS. The Network Configuration Access Control Model provides the means to restrict access for particular users to a preconfigured subset of the available operations and content.

A number of data nodes in the ietf-l2vpn-ntw and ietf-ethernet-segment modules are writable, creatable or deletable, and may be considered sensitive or vulnerable in some network environments. Write and delete operations on these nodes without proper protection or authentication can have a negative effect on network operations. The vpn-profiles container includes sensitive data that influences how the service is delivered: an attacker with access may be able to manipulate routing policies, quality of service policies or encryption properties, which is why these nodes are tagged with default-deny-write. The ethernet-segments and vpn-services containers let an attacker delete a running service and interrupt all of a client's traffic, modify the attributes of a running service or of an Ethernet segment and so cause service malfunction and SLA violations, create an L2VPN service, add a network access, or intercept and redirect traffic to an unauthorized node. Such activity can be detected by adequately monitoring and tracking network configuration changes.

Some readable data nodes may also be sensitive. The customer-name and ip-connection nodes can reveal privacy-related information that can be used to track a customer, and disclosing it may be considered a violation of the customer-provider trust relationship. The two IANA-maintained modules define identities for encapsulation and pseudowire types; they are meant to be referenced by other modules and expose no writable nodes, read-only state or RPCs.
sections.plainLanguage: Writing to these fields changes how the provider's network behaves, so the write access has to be restricted. Reading the customer name may also be sensitive. The model marks the most dangerous parts so that access control rules can deny writes by default.
